drafts.title: The Case of the Hidden Girl
drafts.reasoning: This scene highlights the conflict between Hank’s gruff nature and John's youthful enthusiasm. It also sets up key relationships (like Noel and Sierra) through subtle hints.
drafts.scene: A dimly lit conference room filled with paperwork and police paraphernalia. The temperature is cold, reflecting the tension in the air. John stands nervously by a window overlooking an empty street outside, sipping on stale coffee. Hank enters from another door, carrying a large box labeled 'snacks'. He stops abruptly upon seeing John.

dialogue.line: What are you doing, kid? You're supposed to be out there interviewing witnesses.
I was just—taking a break. I mean, we've been at it all day! Maybe some snacks will help keep me going.
Snacks? You want snacks? Do you realize how much time this case has cost us?
Hey, when I get hungry, I eat. That’s what my mom taught me.
Your mother must have had bad taste if she thought that was good advice.
Maybe you should get a new advisor, Captain. A less salty one.
Alright, alright. Let's focus. Do you know anything about the girl found in Sierra's alley yesterday?
